A security review flagged that visiting a redirect endpoint whose target URL contains CRLF characters causes extra, attacker-controlled headers to appear in the HTTP response. The service is used in production and the codebase spans several modules: a main handler, an auth helper module, a JSON response builder class, and a SQLite storage layer. The developer who wrote it was conscientious about functionality but unaware of header injection risks, so user-supplied values flow into response headers through several different mechanisms without any sanitization.",
  "environment_setup": "The Dockerfile installs curl (for the agent to test with), copies the LinkVault Python package into /app/linkvault/ (files: __init__.py, app.py, auth.py, response.py, store.py), and creates /app/data/ for the SQLite database. No pip packages are needed—only the Python standard library is used. The service starts with `python3 -m linkvault.app` on port 8080.   "instruction_summary": "instruction.md explains that a header injection bug was found in the LinkVault URL shortener: when a short link's target URL contains CRLF (\\r\\n), visiting the redirect causes extra headers in the response. It states the property: 'No user-supplied value can ever put a line break (CR or LF) into any HTTP response header, cookie value, or redirect location. This must hold for every endpoint and every code path.' It tells the agent the service lives in /app/linkvault/, runs on port 8080 via `python3 -m linkvault.app`, and asks them to fix the codebase so the property holds everywhere. It does not mention the number of vulnerable sites, their locations, or their mechanisms.",
  "solution_outline": [
    "Add a _sanitize_header method to LinkVaultHandler that strips \\r and \\n from string values.",
    "Override send_header in LinkVaultHandler to call _sanitize_header on the value before delegating to super().send_header — this covers Sites 1 (redirect Location), 2 (Set-Cookie via auth helper), 3 (X-Request-Id via JSONResponse builder), and 4 (X-Display-Name from DB).",
    "Fix _send_raw_response to sanitize each header value through _sanitize_header before writing the raw header lines to wfile — this covers Site 5 (Content-Disposition via direct wfile.write).",
    "Restart the server and verify no CRLF injection is possible on any endpoint."
  ],
  "test_plan": [
    "test_redirect_no_crlf: Create a short link whose URL contains %0d%0aX-LV-T1:pwned via GET /api/shorten?url=…&request_id=safe, then GET /go/{code} and assert 'X-LV-T1' does not appear in the response headers. Also assert the redirect still works (status 302 or a Location header is present with the URL minus CRLF).",
    "test_cookie_no_crlf: POST /login with username containing %0d%0aX-LV-T2:pwned (wrong password), assert 'X-LV-T2' does not appear in response headers, and assert a Set-Cookie header with 'last_user=' is still present.",
    "test_request_id_no_crlf: GET /api/shorten?url=http://safe.com&request_id=req%0d%0aX-LV-T3:pwned, assert 'X-LV-T3' does not appear in response headers, and assert an X-Request-Id header is still present (with CRLF stripped).",
    "test_display_name_no_crlf: Login as admin/admin123 (cookie jar), POST /api/profile with display_name containing %0d%0aX-LV-T4:pwned, GET /dashboard with session cookie, assert 'X-LV-T4' does not appear in response headers, and assert X-Display-Name header is present (sanitized).",
    "test_export_filename_no_crlf: GET /export?filename=report%0d%0aX-LV-T5:pwned.csv, assert 'X-LV-T5' does not appear in response headers, and assert Content-Disposition header is present (with sanitized filename).",
    "test_clean_redirect_still_works: Create a short link with a clean URL, follow the redirect, assert status 302 and Location header points to the correct URL without any stripping of legitimate characters."
